name: Carousel Studio
summary: Plan a carousel from the first slide to the caption, with a repeatable layout and a review checklist.
audience: Creators and small business owners who write their own social posts.
needs: A text AI assistant and a slide or design editor. Image generation is optional.
includes: 10 prompts for research, hooks and slide copy
sample: Act as a carousel editor. Topic: [TOPIC]. Reader: [AUDIENCE]. Source notes: [VERIFIED NOTES]. Goal: [ONE ACTION]. Draft six slides: a specific opening, the problem, two practical steps, one worked example and a closing action. For each slide give a headline under nine words, body copy under 35 words and one visual direction. Separate any claim needing a source. Finish with a caption and alt text for each slide. Do not invent results or customer quotes.

name: Carousel Workflow Kit
summary: Specify a content queue, review steps and scheduled publishing without losing track of failed posts.
audience: Creators moving from manual posting to a reviewed publishing workflow.
needs: A text AI assistant. Implementing the plans requires your own automation platform and connected publishing accounts.
sample: Design a content queue for [CHANNEL] using [AUTOMATION TOOL]. Store draft_id, content_url, scheduled_at, timezone, approval_state, publish_state, external_post_id and last_error. Only approved rows may publish. Describe states and transitions, a duplicate prevention key, retry rules for timeouts and rate limits, and how an operator reconciles a post that succeeded remotely but timed out locally. Return a table and five acceptance tests. Keep credentials out of the queue. Do not publish anything.

name: 3D Website Lab
summary: Write a build brief for a product site with a 3D scene, mobile fallbacks and a clear route to checkout.
audience: Freelancers and founders building a product landing page with a coding assistant.
needs: An AI coding tool and a browser. Supply your own licensed models, images or video when the brief needs them.
includes: Mobile, keyboard and performance review steps
sample: Inspect my current app before editing. Build a product landing page for [PRODUCT] aimed at [AUDIENCE]. Use [EXISTING STACK]. Start with a readable HTML hero and [PRIMARY CTA]. Add one optional 3D object from [LICENSED ASSET] only after the main content loads. Provide a static poster when WebGL fails, reduced motion is enabled or the device cannot sustain the scene. Keep text and navigation outside the canvas. Return the implementation plan, asset requirements and checks for keyboard access, small screens and loading performance.

name: AI Video Direction Kit
summary: Describe a shot, keep the subject consistent and review generated clips before choosing a final take.
audience: Creators planning generated product clips and short brand films.
needs: A text AI assistant plus your chosen image or video generator. Generation credits are separate.
includes: 10 prompts for shots, continuity and repairs
A take selection and continuity checklist
sample: Turn this brief into a shot specification: [BRIEF]. Use only these product facts: [FACTS]. Describe subject identity, action, camera position, lens feel, lighting, background and duration in separate fields. Make the action physically plausible. Define start and end frames and list details that must stay constant across takes. Provide a shorter fallback prompt if the generator ignores the main action. Finish with a review checklist for geometry, text, hands, reflections and continuity. Do not claim that any take has been generated or tested.

name: UGC Ad Script Kit
summary: Write product demonstration scripts with shot notes, claim checks and clear advertising disclosures.
audience: Small brands briefing a presenter or producing disclosed AI-assisted ads.
needs: A text AI assistant. Filming, voice and video generation tools are optional and sold separately.
includes: Presenter, disclosure and edit review steps
sample: Write a 20-second product demonstration script for [PRODUCT] and [AUDIENCE]. Verified benefits: [FACTS WITH SOURCES]. Presenter: [REAL CONSENTING PRESENTER OR DISCLOSED SYNTHETIC PRESENTER]. Use a problem, a visible demonstration and one CTA. Return timecodes, spoken words, shot instructions and on-screen text. Mark where an ad or synthetic-presenter disclosure belongs. Avoid first-person experience claims unless the presenter supplied them. Flag every benefit that lacks evidence. Keep the script under 50 spoken words.

name: Short Explainer Studio
summary: Turn a source-backed topic into a short visual explanation with a script, shot list and fact check.
audience: Educators and creators making concise explanatory videos.
needs: A text AI assistant, trustworthy topic sources and an editor or video generator.
includes: Narration timing and visual accuracy checks
sample: Explain [TOPIC] to [AUDIENCE] in a 30-second script using only [SOURCE EXCERPTS]. Choose one question and answer it directly. Return a table with time range, narration, visual action and supporting source. Use a simple original visual analogy and state its limits. Keep narration under 70 words. Mark uncertainties instead of filling gaps. End with the answer rather than an unrelated call to action. List any visuals that could misrepresent scale, causation or time.

name: Motion Briefs for Code
summary: Give a coding assistant a precise motion brief with scene timing, reusable variables and export checks.
audience: Developers creating title cards, launch clips or data animations with code.
needs: An AI coding assistant and your chosen animation framework. These are prompts, not finished video templates.
sample: Inspect the animation project and use its existing framework. Create a six-second title card for [TITLE] in [WIDTH x HEIGHT] at [FPS]. Define a single deterministic timeline: title enters at 0.4 seconds, supporting line at 1.2 seconds, both hold until 4.8 seconds, then exit by 5.6 seconds. Expose copy and colors as variables. Use licensed local fonts. Make arbitrary-time seeking produce the same frame as sequential playback. Return file changes and checks at 0, 1.2, 3 and 5.6 seconds. Do not claim a render exists until it has completed.

name: Lyric Visual Planner
summary: Map music you have permission to use to readable lyric cards, beat notes and an export plan.
audience: Musicians and editors preparing lyric clips from their own or licensed tracks.
needs: A text AI assistant, a video editor and a track plus lyrics you have permission to use.
includes: Safe area, contrast and sync checks
sample: Plan a 15-second lyric clip using [AUTHORIZED LYRIC EXCERPT] and [TIMECODES]. Canvas: [RATIO]. Audience: [AUDIENCE]. Return cue in/out times, text groups, line breaks, emphasis and transition notes. Keep every word inside the platform safe area and provide a high-contrast background direction. Do not invent lyrics or timing. If timestamps are missing, return a timing worksheet and label the cut provisional. Include a readability check for a small phone screen.

name: Pixel Brand Prompt Kit
summary: Define a pixel art style for brand characters, icons and small illustrations before generating assets.
audience: Creators and small teams making a consistent pixel art asset set.
needs: A text AI assistant plus a pixel editor or image generator. Manual cleanup may be needed.
includes: 10 prompts for style and asset briefs
Grid, silhouette and small-size review steps
sample: Create a pixel art specification for an original [CHARACTER OR OBJECT] for [BRAND]. Grid: [SIZE]. Palette: [HEX COLORS]. Describe silhouette, proportions, light direction, outline rules and background transparency. Give a generator prompt and a manual cleanup checklist. Keep edges aligned to the pixel grid and avoid blur, gradients and anti-aliasing. Return variations for neutral, active and resting poses using the same proportions. Do not imitate a named artist or an existing character.

name: YouTube Production Planner
summary: Plan a video from research through upload review, with clear human checkpoints for facts and rights.
audience: Solo creators documenting a repeatable YouTube production process.
needs: A text AI assistant and an editor. Scheduling or uploads require your own tools and account setup.
includes: Fact, rights and upload review steps
sample: Design a reviewed production workflow for a [LENGTH]-minute YouTube video about [TOPIC]. Inputs: [SOURCES], [ORIGINAL FOOTAGE], [VOICE RIGHTS] and [CHANNEL STYLE]. Return stages for research, outline, script, assets, edit, captions, thumbnail and upload review. Each stage needs an owner, required input, output, failure condition and approval rule. Keep uploading as a separate manual approval. Add a rights ledger and a fact-check queue. Do not promise views, monetization or ranking.

name: Video Shot Prompt Library
summary: Choose from 30 original shot briefs for product details, small spaces and outdoor scenes.
audience: Creators who want specific starting points for generated B-roll.
needs: A video generator of your choice. Each brief needs your subject and any reference assets you are licensed to use.
includes: A shot review and selection checklist
sample: Create a six-second close-up of [PRODUCT] on a matte stone surface. A large window on camera left provides soft daylight. Begin on the edge texture, then make a slow lateral camera move to reveal the full product. The product stays still and retains the exact shape, finish and markings of [AUTHORIZED REFERENCE]. Keep the background plain and depth of field sufficient to read the product outline. Review the result for drifting labels, changing geometry and implausible reflections before using it.
